requirement:
A `{req}` declaration MAY list `:impl:` and `:test:` options, and an `{example}`
declaration MAY list `:test:` options, immediately after its opening fence and
before its body, one per option line, naming a project file path or
`path#selector` for one outline node under
{cite}`requirements.references.outline_selectors`. Each anchor MUST be an `{impl}` or `{test}` edge, under
{cite}`requirements.references.targets`, from the definition to the anchored file or
node, for files that cannot or should not carry a reference themselves.
Paths MUST follow the path rules in {cite}`requirements.ci.schema`. Option lines
MUST NOT form part of the definition's text for evidence comparison or for
requirements inputs, and MUST NOT render as body text.

An anchored file or node MUST be covered by the definition's evidence under
{cite}`requirements.references.evidence_coverage`, by an input selecting it, so changing the file makes that evidence stale. A path or selector that
does not resolve to a readable, permitted file or node MUST be a validation error naming the
definition and the path; authoring MUST report it before inference, because the
definition cannot be assessed without it. Any other option line in a `{req}` or
`{example}` declaration MUST be a validation error.

Agents SHOULD NOT anchor a file when a more precise reference is available, such
as a reference attached to the Rust item that implements or tests the
definition. Habeas's bundled agent skills MUST give this direction.
rationale:
I judge that the sources satisfy `requirements.references.anchors`. No FIXME acknowledgements apply, and I found no unacknowledged gaps. I read the code and tests but did not run them.

**Parsing and edges**
- `definition_blocks` in `src/lib.rs` parses `:name: value` option lines (`option_line`) immediately after a `{req}` or `{example}` opening fence. It stops at the first non-option line, so a later `:test:` in the body is not an option. The test `anchor_options_are_metadata_not_body_text` covers this.
- `collect_definitions` in `src/evidence.rs` maps `:impl:` on a requirement to an Impl edge and `:test:` on a requirement or example to a Test edge. `Anchor::parse` splits `path#selector`.
- Any other option name, including `:impl:` on an example, and any option with an empty value are validation errors. `unsupported_and_empty_options_are_validation_errors` covers both.

**Option lines excluded from text**
- `without_options` removes option lines from the definition text, from `raw_lines` (requirements inputs), and from `preprocess_book`.
- `replace_definitions` renders from `text_start`, so option lines do not appear as body text.
- Tests: `requirements_inputs_omit_option_lines`, `anchor_options_are_metadata_not_body_text`, `every_definition_gets_a_nested_detail_page_without_an_index`, and the "text changed" assertion in `anchored_files_must_be_completely_covered_and_resolvable`.

**Evidence coverage**
- `validate_references` resolves each anchor and requires an outline input that selects the anchored node or one of its ancestors. Otherwise it reports "no input selects … anchored by :impl:".
- `anchored_files_must_be_completely_covered_and_resolvable` shows that a descendant section does not cover the root. It also shows that changing the anchored file makes the evidence stale.
- `selector_anchors_are_covered_by_inputs_selecting_the_node_or_an_ancestor` covers sibling, exact, parent and root inputs.

**Unresolvable anchors**
- Validation reports an error naming the definition, the anchor path and the declaration location (`validate_references`; tested).
- Authoring fails in `AssessmentSources::prepare` before inference, with "`<name>`: cannot read :impl: anchor `<path>`". A missing file and an `[evidence] disallow`-denied path are both tested in `unreadable_or_denied_anchors_fail_before_inference`. The denied case returns `PermissionDenied`.
- `prepare` also adds each anchor as a mandatory outline input. `anchored_files_contribute_root_node_inputs` and `references_contribute_their_owning_outline_nodes` cover this.

**Related surfaces**
- The `references` tool reports anchors as file or node sites (`references_report_anchors_as_file_or_node_sites`). `DefinitionEdges::current` in `src/index.rs` groups anchored inputs as implementation or tests (`detail_inputs_are_grouped_by_current_edges_in_disclosures`). Both are marked `{impl}` and `{test}`.

**Skills direction**
- `assets/skills/habeas-requirements/SKILL.md` is anchored with `:impl:` in `md/requirements/references.md`. It says "Do not anchor a file when a more precise reference is available, such as a comment attached to the Rust item".
- The bootstrap and evidence skills do not repeat this, but the bootstrap skill defers to `habeas-requirements` for directive syntax. I accepted that as meeting the "bundled agent skills MUST give this direction" obligation. A strict reading of "skills" in the plural could ask for it in all three; I did not.

**Marking and unspecified behavior**
- The `{impl}` markings cover the structs, helpers and parse/validate functions involved.
- I found no unmarked code that implements part of the requirement. I found no behavior in the marked code beyond what this requirement and its cited requirements specify.

:::{req} outline_selectors
An outline selector MUST be a `/`-separated path of segments from the file's
root node to an outline node; the empty selector MUST select the root node. A
named node's segment MUST be `kind[name]`. An anonymous node's segment MUST be
`kind@hash`, where `hash` is the first twelve hexadecimal digits of its identity
hash under {cite}`requirements.references.structural_hash`. Siblings whose
segments would otherwise be identical MUST be disambiguated by `#N`, their
one-based position among those siblings in source order, except `line` nodes:
identical lines are interchangeable, so a `line` selector MUST resolve when any
line with that content exists in the file. In names, `%`, `[`, `]`, `/`, `#`,
`@`, and whitespace MUST be percent-encoded as UTF-8 bytes, so selectors are
reversible. Line numbers MUST NOT form part of a selector.
:::{req} targets

Project text files MAY use the `{impl}`, `{cite}`, and `{test}` roles with a backtick-delimited full requirement or example name. Each reference is a directed edge between its source and the named definition. A source is a project source item or a requirement or example declaration. `{cite}` MUST mean that the source relies on, supports, or refers to the definition, and is an edge from the source to the definition. `{impl}` MUST mean that the source implements part of the definition: it makes a decision, performs a check, produces an output, or handles a case that the definition specifies. A requirement MAY implement part of another requirement by refining one of its obligations. Calling code that implements a definition, or producing a result a caller uses to meet it, MUST NOT by itself count as implementing it. A requirement stating a convention for every output of a kind, such as every validation error, is implemented by the source that carries out the convention as a whole, such as the step that collects and reports those outputs. `{test}` MUST mean that the source is designed to verify behavior the definition specifies: a test through its scenario and the assertions about that scenario's outcome, or a named example through the concrete case it describes. `{impl}` and `{test}` are edges from the definition to the source. Only requirements and examples are assessed; code is reviewed as part of the definitions it implements or tests. Habeas MUST find these references throughout project source files and MUST fail with the source file and line if a name has no matching `{req}` or `{example}` definition. In Markdown, escaped roles and roles in code examples MUST remain literal. Evidence snapshots and generated build output MUST NOT be counted as additional source references.
```text
{impl}`requirements.references.targets`
{cite}`requirements.references.targets`
{test}`requirements.references.targets`
:::{req} schema

A requirement or example evidence file at `evidence/<full-name>.json` MUST be a JSON object with exactly `requirement` or `example`, `determination`, `rationale`, and `inputs`. The definition text and rationale MUST be nonempty strings, `determination` MUST use one of the outcomes defined by {cite}`requirements.ci.outcomes`, and `inputs` MUST be an array. Every evidence input MUST have exactly one of three forms: an outline input with `file`, `item`, and `hash`; a requirements input with `requirements`, `matches`, and `text`; or a definition input with `definition` and `text`. File paths MUST resolve to permitted inputs under {cite}`requirements.ci.input_containment`. Project-local paths SHOULD be recorded relative to the project for portability; absolute and parent-relative paths MAY be used when their resolved targets are permitted. `matches` MUST be an array of distinct full definition names, `hash` MUST be a lowercase hexadecimal SHA-256 digest, and `text` MUST be a nonempty array of strings. Evidence MUST NOT store source text for outline inputs.
:::{req} evidence_coverage

For every `{impl}` and `{test}` reference in a project source file, including one in a requirement or example declaration, the evidence file for the referenced requirement or example MUST contain an input whose resolved source ranges cover the reference's file and line. A `{cite}` reference MUST NOT require coverage; it is discoverable through {cite}`requirements.authoring.reference_index`. Habeas MUST report every uncovered reference with its role, full name, source file, and line number.
